Through sponsorships, partnerships and research collaborations, the Chair co-produces applied knowledge and tools that support ecological, economic and social transitions at the local level. Patronage Patrons and Partners Academic Collaborations Our Patrons and Partners Updated on 21/01/2026 Presentation | Research | Observatories | Education and Training | News and Press | Partnerships Patronage By supporting a research chair, you contribute to the development of applied research with concrete impact for ecosystems engaged in sustainability transitions. You also support and take part in the advancement of innovative educational approaches addressing these challenges. Partners benefit from privileged access to research teams, academic expertise, students and the international reputation of Grenoble Ecole de Management. Why engage as a patron? While the Chair’s research outputs are made widely accessible, supporting the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair enables you to: Contribute to shaping and validating the Chair’s strategic research priorities Deepen understanding of emerging phenomena affecting organisations and local socio-economic systems Participate in working groups aligned with your organisation’s interests Increase your organisation’s visibility through Chair publications and events Build strong connections with GEM’s educational programmes and students Patrons and Partners The Chair develops several types of partnerships. These may involve collaboration on a shared project, funding a postdoctoral position focused on a specific research theme, or jointly supervising a CIFRE PhD thesis (in French) with a partner organisation. Academic Collaborations The Chair collaborates with a wide range of academic institutions on joint research projects, including participation in the POPSU programme (in French) on attractiveness and later on water-related pathways; the Annual Report on Risks and Resilience (in French); scientific advisory boards for Grenoble European Green Capital initiatives and the Climate and Transitions Scientific Council (in French). The Chair also co-organises public-facing events with research institutions. Our Patrons and Partners The Chair operates through three partner groups: one bringing together local and regional public authorities, one composed of companies, and a third group made up of actors from the social and solidarity economy (SSE). The third group includes partners with whom the Chair engages in shared expertise and knowledge exchange. Public Authorities Group Corporate Partners Group Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) Group Expertise and Knowledge-Sharing Partners Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair Presentation How can local areas be supported in their ecological, economic and social transitions towards a more sustainable future and improved local well-being? The Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM mobilises scientific and partnership-based research to observe, understand and accelerate local and regional transitions. By bringing together researchers, businesses and public authorities, the Chair develops applied research on lifestyles, local public policies, sustainable economic models and local well-being, placing research at the service of action and societal impact. Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair Research Research conducted within the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM examines transformations in lifestyles, organizational forms and economic models at the local scale, with the aim of supporting ecological, economic and social transitions towards more sustainable pathways and enhanced well-being. Structured around four complementary research streams, the Chair’s work combines empirical investigations, applied research and experimental approaches. It results in reports for a broad audience, academic publications and doctoral supervision, while being firmly embedded in a collaborative research dynamic closely connected to public authorities and economic actors. Research Observatories In response to today’s ecological and social transition challenges, the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair develops observatories designed to better understand local dynamics and support collective action. The Well-being Resource Hub and the Transitions Barometer provide insights into practices, perceptions and value creation, helping identify new levers to support fairer and more sustainable transition pathways. Observatories Education and Training The Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at Grenoble École de Management bridges impact-driven research and education, across both degree programmes and executive education. Through courses, pedagogical projects, serious games and case studies, the Chair equips students and professionals to address ecological, economic and social transitions within local systems. Through sponsorships, partnerships and research collaborations, the Chair co-produces applied knowledge and tools that support ecological, economic and social transitions at the local level. Patronage Patrons and Partners Academic Collaborations Our Patrons and Partners Updated on 21/01/2026 Presentation | Research | Observatories | Education and Training | News and Press | Partnerships Patronage By supporting a research chair, you contribute to the development of applied research with concrete impact for ecosystems engaged in sustainability transitions. You also support and take part in the advancement of innovative educational approaches addressing these challenges. Partners benefit from privileged access to research teams, academic expertise, students and the international reputation of Grenoble Ecole de Management. Why engage as a patron? While the Chair’s research outputs are made widely accessible, supporting the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair enables you to: Contribute to shaping and validating the Chair’s strategic research priorities Deepen understanding of emerging phenomena affecting organisations and local socio-economic systems Participate in working groups aligned with your organisation’s interests Increase your organisation’s visibility through Chair publications and events Build strong connections with GEM’s educational programmes and students Patrons and Partners The Chair develops several types of partnerships. These may involve collaboration on a shared project, funding a postdoctoral position focused on a specific research theme, or jointly supervising a CIFRE PhD thesis (in French) with a partner organisation. Academic Collaborations The Chair collaborates with a wide range of academic institutions on joint research projects, including participation in the POPSU programme (in French) on attractiveness and later on water-related pathways; the Annual Report on Risks and Resilience (in French); scientific advisory boards for Grenoble European Green Capital initiatives and the Climate and Transitions Scientific Council (in French). The Chair also co-organises public-facing events with research institutions. Our Patrons and Partners The Chair operates through three partner groups: one bringing together local and regional public authorities, one composed of companies, and a third group made up of actors from the social and solidarity economy (SSE). The third group includes partners with whom the Chair engages in shared expertise and knowledge exchange. Public Authorities Group Corporate Partners Group Social and Solidarity Economy (SSE) Group Expertise and Knowledge-Sharing Partners Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair Presentation How can local areas be supported in their ecological, economic and social transitions towards a more sustainable future and improved local well-being? The Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM mobilises scientific and partnership-based research to observe, understand and accelerate local and regional transitions. By bringing together researchers, businesses and public authorities, the Chair develops applied research on lifestyles, local public policies, sustainable economic models and local well-being, placing research at the service of action and societal impact. Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair Research Research conducted within the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM examines transformations in lifestyles, organizational forms and economic models at the local scale, with the aim of supporting ecological, economic and social transitions towards more sustainable pathways and enhanced well-being. Structured around four complementary research streams, the Chair’s work combines empirical investigations, applied research and experimental approaches. It results in reports for a broad audience, academic publications and doctoral supervision, while being firmly embedded in a collaborative research dynamic closely connected to public authorities and economic actors. Research Observatories In response to today’s ecological and social transition challenges, the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair develops observatories designed to better understand local dynamics and support collective action. The Well-being Resource Hub and the Transitions Barometer provide insights into practices, perceptions and value creation, helping identify new levers to support fairer and more sustainable transition pathways. Observatories Education and Training The Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at Grenoble École de Management bridges impact-driven research and education, across both degree programmes and executive education. Through courses, pedagogical projects, serious games and case studies, the Chair equips students and professionals to address ecological, economic and social transitions within local systems. The Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM mobilises scientific and partnership-based research to observe, understand and accelerate local and regional transitions. By bringing together researchers, businesses and public authorities, the Chair develops applied research on lifestyles, local public policies, sustainable economic models and local well-being, placing research at the service of action and societal impact. Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair Research Research conducted within the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair at GEM examines transformations in lifestyles, organizational forms and economic models at the local scale, with the aim of supporting ecological, economic and social transitions towards more sustainable pathways and enhanced well-being. Structured around four complementary research streams, the Chair’s work combines empirical investigations, applied research and experimental approaches. It results in reports for a broad audience, academic publications and doctoral supervision, while being firmly embedded in a collaborative research dynamic closely connected to public authorities and economic actors. Research Observatories In response to today’s ecological and social transition challenges, the Local Sustainability Transition and Well-being Chair develops observatories designed to better understand local dynamics and support collective action. The Well-being Resource Hub and the Transitions Barometer provide insights into practices, perceptions and value creation, helping identify new levers to support fairer and more sustainable transition pathways.
